dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each natural number n, this is the inductive type of admissible run records described by constructor D005. A run packages a positive dimension, an abstract matrix norm, scalar parameters, seven real n-by-n matrices, inherited-error bounds, a product decomposition, and several norm inequalities.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target quantifies over every n and every admissible run of dimension n, so all fields and proof fields packaged by this type are assumptions of the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this proposition is the conjunction N(A times DeltaB) <= N(A)e_R and S = T + (R + L), where T = mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B), R = N(A)e_R, L = e_L N(B), and S is defined to be T + (R + L).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This definition supplies the complete conclusion. Its second conjunct becomes a reflexive equality after unfolding the component definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the value-function projection of a LocalDef011 norm record: it maps an n-by-n real matrix to its real-valued norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the meaning of every occurrence of run.matrixNorm.value as evaluation of the selected abstract matrix norm N.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the matrix-norm record from an admissible run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects the norm N used in both conclusions and in the bundled assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor builds a run from: n with 0 < n; a matrix norm N; epsilon > 0; a nonnegative function mu on the natural numbers; a natural degree d; a nonnegative real growth constant C satisfying mu(k) <= C(k as a real)^d for every k; matrices A, B, DeltaA, DeltaB, P, E, and H; nonnegative reals e_L, e_R, and c_H; the identity P = (((A + DeltaA)(B + DeltaB)) + E) + H; and bounds N(E) <= mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B), N(DeltaA) <= e_L, N(DeltaB) <= e_R, and N(H) <= c_H epsilon^2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the theorem conditional on this entire data package. The first target inequality directly relies only on norm nonnegativity and submultiplicativity together with N(DeltaB) <= e_R; most other constructor assumptions do not occur in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines S = mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B) + (N(A)e_R + e_L N(B)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the left side of the target's equality and expands to exactly the expression on the right side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines the left-inherited contribution L = e_L N(B).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the final summand in the target equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines the matrix product A times DeltaB, where A is exactLeft and DeltaB is rightPerturbation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its norm is the left side of the nontrivial target inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines the right-inherited contribution R = N(A)e_R.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is both the upper bound for N(A times DeltaB) and the middle summand in the target equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines the local contribution T = mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the leading summand on the right side of the target equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each n, this is the inductive type of abstract real-valued norms on n-by-n real matrices, with the norm axioms supplied by constructor D021.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A run contains one such norm; its nonnegativity and submultiplicativity support the first conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the positive real epsilon from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Epsilon appears in the local contribution mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B) and in bundled error assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the exact-left n-by-n real matrix A from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A occurs in N(A times DeltaB), N(A), and the local and inherited scalar contributions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the exact-right n-by-n real matrix B from a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: B occurs through N(B) in the local and left-inherited contributions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the nonnegative left inherited-error bound e_L.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It contributes the term e_L N(B) to the target equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the function mu from natural numbers to real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its value mu(n) is a factor in the local contribution appearing in the target equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the nonnegative right inherited-error bound e_R.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the upper bound N(A)e_R in the first conclusion and the corresponding term in the equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the right-perturbation n-by-n real matrix DeltaB.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the second factor of the matrix product whose norm is bounded in the first conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each n, this is the type of matrices indexed by Fin n in both directions with real entries, namely real n-by-n matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes all matrix quantities in the run and conclusion to be square and dimension-compatible.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary matrix multiplication for real n-by-n matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines A times DeltaB in the first conclusion and the product of perturbed factors in the bundled computed-product identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor forms a matrix norm N satisfying: N(X) >= 0; N(X) = 0 iff X = 0; N(cX) = |c|N(X); N(X + Y) <= N(X) + N(Y); and N(XY) <= N(X)N(Y), for all appropriately quantified real scalars and n-by-n real matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Submultiplicativity yields N(A DeltaB) <= N(A)N(DeltaB), and nonnegativity of N(A) permits use of N(DeltaB) <= e_R to obtain the first conclusion.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, implicit in the Lean declaration.
N is an abstract real-valued norm on real n-by-n matrices.
epsilon, C, e_L, e_R, and c_H are real scalars; d is a natural number; and mu is a function from natural numbers to real numbers.

A, B, DeltaA, DeltaB, P, E, and H are real n-by-n matrices, representing exact-left, exact-right, left-perturbation, right-perturbation, computed-product, local-first-order-error, and higher-order-remainder quantities.
The target universally quantifies over the single run record that packages all of this data and its assumptions; there are no existentially quantified witnesses.
hypotheses: The function N is nonnegative, definite, absolutely homogeneous, subadditive, and submultiplicative: N(X) >= 0; N(X) = 0 iff X = 0; N(cX) = |c|N(X); N(X + Y) <= N(X) + N(Y); and N(XY) <= N(X)N(Y).
The growth constant satisfies C >= 0, and for every natural k, mu(k) <= C(k as a real)^d.
The inherited-error bounds and remainder coefficient satisfy e_L >= 0, e_R >= 0, and c_H >= 0.
The computed matrix satisfies the exact packaged identity P = (((A + DeltaA)(B + DeltaB)) + E) + H.
The local first-order error satisfies N(E) <= mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B).
The perturbations satisfy N(DeltaA) <= e_L and N(DeltaB) <= e_R.
The higher-order remainder satisfies N(H) <= c_H epsilon^2.
conclusions: mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B) + (N(A)e_R + e_L N(B)) = mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B) + (N(A)e_R + e_L N(B)).
mathematical_definitions: All matrices are functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real, hence square real n-by-n matrices.
Matrix multiplication is standard row-column multiplication with a finite sum over Fin n.
Define T = mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B), R = N(A)e_R, and L = e_L N(B).
LocalDef006 is the scalar S = T + (R + L); LocalDef010, LocalDef009, and LocalDef007 are respectively T, R, and L.
LocalDef008 is the matrix product A DeltaB.
The second conclusion is therefore S = T + (R + L), which is true by unfolding S.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension n and every admissible run containing the stated norm, parameters, matrices, decomposition, and error assumptions, the norm of the product of the exact-left matrix A with the right perturbation DeltaB is at most the norm of A times the right inherited-error bound e_R. In conjunction with this inequality, the proposition states that the defined scalar sum mu(n)epsilon N(A)N(B) + (N(A)e_R + e_L N(B)) equals its own fully expanded definition.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: A constructed run requires 0 < n, so the universal statement is vacuous at n = 0.
More generally, because the theorem quantifies over admissible run records rather than arbitrary raw data, it is vacuous for any n for which no package satisfying all constructor assumptions exists.
The matrix norm is abstract and is not identified as any particular standard norm; only the five supplied norm axioms are encoded.
All matrices are square n-by-n real matrices. No rectangular or complex-matrix case is encoded.
The positivity assumption on epsilon has no encoded upper bound, such as epsilon < 1.
The growth assumptions impose nonnegativity and mu(k) <= Ck^d but do not encode monotonicity of mu or any relation between d and n.
The second conjunct is definitionally reflexive and provides no additional mathematical estimate.
The computed-product identity, the local-error and remainder bounds, the left perturbation, the growth degree and constant, and most positivity assumptions do not affect the stated conclusions.
The proposition bounds only N(A DeltaB). It does not bound DeltaA B, DeltaA DeltaB, the full product perturbation, the computed product P, or a total forward or backward error.
The inherited-error scalars e_L and e_R are only upper bounds on perturbation norms; the proposition does not assert that they equal those norms.
No existential witness, uniqueness assertion, optimality claim, asymptotic statement, or claim that the displayed scalar sum bounds a computed error is encoded.
